title: Student Detonates School Server Room After Teacher Claims C# Superior to C++
subtitle: What began as a routine programming lecture ended in structural damage, three fire trucks, and one exceptionally strong opinion about manual memory management.
excerpt: The device is being described only as “improvised” and “deeply against several handbook policies.” The chess club's tournament bracket did not survive.
author: By Owen Castellano

bodyHTML:
Fourth period AP Computer Science at a school The Silicon Wire has agreed not to name ended Tuesday with three fire engines, a evacuated science wing, and a server room reduced to what the district's incident report describes only as “non-recoverable.” The trigger, according to eleven separate student accounts that all agree on this one detail: the teacher said C# was better than C++.

Witnesses say the student in question, a junior known to classmates mainly for correcting people's Big O notation unprompted, sat in total silence for the remainder of the period. He returned after lunch carrying a covered tray from the chemistry lab, walked directly to the server closet adjoining the CS room, and closed the door. The device that followed is not being described in any technical detail by this publication, the school, or apparently anyone who was actually qualified to describe it — official statements refer to it only as “improvised” and “deeply against several handbook policies.”

"In thirty-one years as a fire marshal I have never once had to ask a school principal to explain what 'manual memory management' means, and I sincerely hope I never do again."
— County Fire Marshal, on scene

No one was injured. The server room, which hosted the district's grading portal, the robotics team's shared drive, and — in what students have called "the real tragedy" — the only unsaved copy of the chess club's tournament bracket, was not so lucky.

The Student Stands By It

Reached by this publication through an intermediary (his mother, who confiscated his phone but relayed one message on his behalf), the student declined to apologize for the outcome, only for "the property damage part, specifically."

The teacher at the center of the dispute has since amended the syllabus to remove all mentions of language preference entirely, replacing the relevant slide with a single line: "Both languages are fine. Please just use whichever one doesn't result in a fire marshal visit."

The district has not commented on whether it plans to press charges, but did confirm that Server Room B will be relocated to a windowless interior room going forward, "for reasons that should be obvious to everyone at this point."
